category: D-RELEASE-1.0 §11 classification of every OPEN issue. Columns: issue, category, reason, owner. The gate scripts/check_release_blockers.sh cross-checks this ledger against the GitHub labels; drift is RED. Categories: 1.0-blocks | 1.0-outside | post-1.0 | not-a-bug | tracking/contract.

reason: Feature — reading text from documents (PDF/`documento.texto`); explicitly OUTSIDE the 0.5.0 scope and the 1.0 core surface, tracked under the official-packages plan (R1/interop-first, experimental). Real issue, accepted after 1.0.

Feature request (rule-6 decision) — `kof.io` has no `realPath`/reparse-point primitive: `isSymlink()` is false for a Windows directory junction, so a confinement check has no portable mechanism. New stdlib surface, outside the 1.0 core; registered as a DECISION REQUEST in `docs/development/README.md` §3.

Core frontend soundness: a bare `Handle` declared type emitted `LHandle;` and died at load with `NoClassDefFoundError: Handle` (FIX LANDED 04/10, `known-bugs` §594). RESIDUAL OPEN: returning `process.spawn(...)` (boxed `java.lang.Long`) from a `Handle`-typed function still compiles clean and fails at load `VerifyError: Bad return type`, because `TypeChecker.isAssignable`'s conservative `ClassType→ClassType` fallback does not refuse a builtin→builtin mismatch; tightening it (and the nameability of the process handle) is a maintainer rule-6 call. Row stays `1.0-blocks` until closed.

Core contract violation: `kof.http` failures (connection refused, non-2xx) surface as raw Java exceptions (`java.net.ConnectException` / `IOException: HTTP 501`) that `catch (String e)` cannot see, contradicting the frozen "Kof throws Strings" contract (`learn/14-exceptions.md`); the program dies with no catch and no `after`. Implementation differs from the Kof contract = bug; 1.0 blocker.

Core JS codegen: a class with two constructors emits only the MAX-ARITY constructor (`JsClassEmitter` drops the rest), so on JS every `Guard(1)` call runs the 2-arg constructor with the extra parameter undefined — `TypeError: Cannot read property 'lines' of undefined` (JVM dispatches by arity correctly). Constructor overload dispatch on JS is core correctness; 1.0 blocker. FIX LANDED 04/10 (`known-bugs` §595, `ConstructorOverloadE2ETest` + arity/type Node repros green) — row stays `1.0-blocks` until the issue is closed.

Security contract + docs: `secrets.get`/`secrets.secret` read a RAW env var (`System.getenv(name)`, `kof_sec_secret_get`) with no `KOF_` prefix and no config fallback, while `learn/stdlib/secrets.md` promised `env KOF_DB_PASSWORD > config`. DOCS HALF FIXED 04/10 (EN+PT comment + bullet corrected to the raw-getenv truth). RESIDUAL OPEN (rule-6): `secrets.secret(unset)` silently returns an empty `Secret` (blank credential) — error vs nullable is a maintainer call. Row stays `1.0-blocks` until closed.

Feature (rule-6 decision): `kof.net` has no name-resolution primitive (`net.resolve` 0 hits) and `kof.http` rejects a caller `Host` header (`restricted header name`), so an egress policy cannot pin a vetted address while keeping the name for Host/SNI/cert checks. New stdlib surface + cross-target policy face, outside the 1.0 core; registered as a DECISION REQUEST.

Core cross-target diagnostic contract: JVM interop (`import java.X`) on Native emits real `java_*` calls and dies at LINK with `undefined reference to java_io_File_init_1` / `java_util_Scanner_nextLine` (`COMP001`) instead of a named compile-time refusal. `known-bugs` §510/`INTEROP003` covers only the external-class STATIC FIELD face; the constructor (`new File(...)`) and instance-method (`sc.nextLine()`) faces leak to the linker. Rule 5/R6 (parity or named diagnostic); 1.0 blocker.

Permanent compatibility-contract issue: the 20 KOF commandments (valid Kof remains valid, compiler regressions belong to the compiler, backends preserve frontend semantics, explicit non-breaking deprecation). No code change is owed; the contract is already represented by AGENTS/DECISIONS/quality gates and the issue must remain open as living doctrine (maintainer 04/10).
